//: Assertions in tests/ whose two sides both fold to compile-time constants, and which are
deliberately about arithmetic or about JavaScript rather than about this repository.
scripts/check-inert-assertions.mjs fails on any inert assertion that is absent from this file,
so a test that cannot fail has to be declared deliberately instead of being discovered years
later. It ALSO fails on any entry here that matches nothing, so an exemption cannot outlive the
assertion it excused: fix or delete the assertion and the licence has to go with it.
An entry is a statement that the assertion makes no claim about this repository. It is NOT a
way to stop the gate asking. If the assertion's title describes src/ -- a count of enum
members, of files, of registry rows -- then the fix is to make a side read that, not to write
a line here. The four that prompted this gate all had correct numbers and no reader:
and 20+7 === 27), and payloads.test.ts (two local constants summed to 27 under a title that
claimed to have counted the payload directory).
The key is the file plus the assertion text with whitespace collapsed, so it survives the
assertion moving lines and stops matching the moment the assertion itself changes.

exempt.tests/types/EnvelopeCap.test.ts :: expec: A fact about JavaScript, not about this SDK: String.length counts UTF-16 code units, so an astral character measures 2 there and 4 as UTF-8 bytes. It sits directly under expect(envelopeByteLength('😀')).toBe(4) and exists to be read against it -- the contrast is the point, and deriving either side would destroy it. The envelope cap is measured in bytes because the broker measures the packet; a cap checked with String.length would pass a frame the broker then drops.
exempt.tests/types/common.test.ts :: expect(emp: The assertion here is the ANNOTATION on the line above -- const empty: MeterValues = {} -- which stops compiling the moment any field of MeterValues stops being optional, which is exactly what the test title claims. The expect is a runtime no-op that adds nothing and takes nothing away. The reader that can fail is `npm run typecheck`, which CI runs as its own job.
